messages:
maria: Hey @leo, quick thread to capture our asks for the EDP follow-up. We need to lock in both financial and availability guarantees for regional reserved GPUs.
leo (cloud-sales): Thanks Maria — got the summary you sent. What specifically do you want in the contract?
maria: Three concrete asks: 1) concurrency floor per-region (not just global), 2) failover/burst across regions with guaranteed credit, 3) meter granularity and reconciliation window tightened.
ajay: For finance: we need a sliding credit if they underdeliver capacity vs committed baseline. Propose pro-rated credits for >2% monthly shortfall, escalates after 4 hours of outage.
katie: Legal: define "available" precisely. Propose: "available" = healthy, schedulable GPUs representing >= concurrency_floor for 95% of 5m windows in the month. Also add audit right to fetch utilization logs.
sam: From SRE: we care about cross-region failover latency and warm standby. If they force preemption for >30% of our instances in a region during peak, we need guaranteed burst capacity in next region within 15 minutes.
maria: Also want a soft cap on egress/networking costs for cross-region failover during incidents — we can't be surprised by a big bill. Ask: capped overage or credit applied.
leo (cloud-sales): I can push those, but vendor typically resists per-region floors. They'll ask for a global minimum. Any tolerance?
ajay: We can accept a hybrid: guarantee a minimum per-region for our primary 3 regions (us-east, eu-west, ap-southeast) and a lower global floor for the rest. Example: 200 GPU concurrency floor per primary region, 500 global reserve.
maria: Exactly. And include a rollback clause: if they move capacity due to maintenance, they must provide equivalent replacement within 2h or issue credits.
contract-bot: Reminder: attach redlines with clause numbers. Use template 'edp-rg-2026-v1' as base.
katie: I'll prepare a redline focusing on definitions, metrics, and the audit right. Also add an SLA table with remedies: credit = min(monthly_commitment * shortfall_pct * 0.5, $ cap).
sam: Can we get monitoring hooks? e.g., a public endpoint or telemetry feed for real-time capacity state so our autoscaler can see vendor capacity flags.
leo (cloud-sales): They may provide a push webhook or CloudHealth metric feed. I'll ask for a subset: capacity_state.{region,zone} with values {green,yellow,red}.
ajay: Billing reconciliation: require per-minute billing for reserved pool rather than hourly, and a 60-day audit window for invoice disputes. Also require CSV export of metering that matches our internal usage ids.
maria: Last thing — ask for a short trial of the regional floor (30 days) at a discounted attach rate so we can validate failover ops before committing long term.
leo (cloud-sales): Ok I'll take these to my counterpart. Expect initial response by EOD Fri. I'll push the 3-region floor ask and the 15m failover SLA as priority.
maria: Thanks. If they push back hard, fallback negotiation: higher financial commitment for a stronger SLA, or a monthly escrow credit pool.
katie: Noted. I'll loop legal into the next thread and draft redlines.
sam: I'll prepare a short ops runbook for the 30-day trial and test failover steps.
ajay: I'll model the proposed credit formula in the financial plan and share numbers tomorrow.
leo (cloud-sales): Got it. Will update thread after vendor response. :thumbsup:
maria: Great — tagging next steps: @katie redline, @sam runbook, @ajay finance model. We'll align Friday 10am PT.
leo (cloud-sales): Confirmed.
